_about: Published empirical rainfall thresholds for landslide initiation, used by SANKET until a model trained on real event data exists. ratio = observed rainfall / threshold rainfall for the same duration; the largest ratio over all evaluated durations governs.

levels.note: ratio >= 1.0 means rainfall has reached conditions under which landslides were recorded in the source study (these are lower-bound thresholds). The 2x (warning) and 4x (danger) multiples are SANKET operational settings, NOT published values: calibrate them with the History page.

uttarakhand_himalaya.label: Garhwal-Kumaon Himalaya (Uttarakhand)
uttarakhand_himalaya.basis: Lower boundary of 81 landslide-triggering rainfall events, Chamoli-Joshimath region, daily rain-gauge data (so only durations >= 24 h are evaluated).
uttarakhand_himalaya.citation: Kanungo, D.P. & Sharma, S. (2014). Rainfall thresholds for prediction of shallow landslides around Chamoli-Joshimath region, Garhwal Himalayas, India. Landslides 11(4), 629-638.

kerala_western_ghats.label: Western Ghats (Kerala)
kerala_western_ghats.basis: Idukki district rainfall and landslide records 2010-2018, daily data (durations >= 24 h).
kerala_western_ghats.citation: Abraham, M.T., Pothuraju, D. & Satyam, N. (2019). Rainfall Thresholds for Prediction of Landslides in Idukki, India: An Empirical Approach. Water 11(10), 2113.

darjeeling_sikkim.label: Darjeeling-Sikkim Himalaya
darjeeling_sikkim.basis: Kalimpong, catalogue of 61 landslide events, frequentist approach.
darjeeling_sikkim.citation: Dikshit, A. & Satyam, N. (2018). Estimation of rainfall thresholds for landslide occurrences in Kalimpong, India. Innovative Infrastructure Solutions.

northeast_himalaya.label: North-Eastern Himalaya
northeast_himalaya.basis: 490 rain-driven landslides 2006-2019; cumulative event rainfall E (mm) vs duration D (h), valid 24 < D < 1440 h.
northeast_himalaya.citation: Monga, D. & Ganguli, P. (2024). Northeast Indian Himalaya rainfall thresholds. Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences Discussions, preprint nhess-2024-152.
northeast_himalaya.status: preprint (in open discussion, not final peer-reviewed)

global_default.label: Global threshold (Guzzetti et al. 2008) - no regional threshold for this state
global_default.basis: Global lower-bound threshold from 2,626 rainfall events that triggered shallow landslides and debris flows. Coefficients as widely cited; replace with a regional threshold for these states when one is verified.
global_default.citation: Guzzetti, F., Peruccacci, S., Rossi, M. & Stark, C.P. (2008). The rainfall intensity-duration control of shallow landslides and debris flows: an update. Landslides 5(1), 3-17.

terrain_gate.note: The published thresholds are only applied where a hillside exists: the steepest 150 m-mean slope within 1 km (Copernicus GLO-30) must be >= 12 deg. Basis: at 178 precisely mapped landslide sites (Kerala 2018, Himachal 2023) that value was >= 17.7 deg at 99% of sites and 8.6 deg at the lowest; flat plains (e.g. Sehore, 10.4 deg) fall below it.
